plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the two rotation operations on a binary search tree as a pair of small subtree drawings joined by dotted arrows. On the right, the upper node is a gray circle labeled x with a short stub edge rising to an unnamed parent; x's left edge ends at the Greek letter alpha, and its right edge descends to a second gray circle labeled y whose two edges end at beta and gamma. On the left stands the other configuration: y is now the upper node holding the parent stub, x is y's left child, and the edges terminate at alpha and beta below x and at gamma below y. Subtrees appear only as these labeled edges, without triangles. Between the drawings, an upper dotted arrow points leftward with "LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)" set above it, and a lower dotted arrow points rightward with "RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y)" set beneath it. Placing the before and after shapes side by side isolates what a rotation touches, the link joining x and y and which of them owns the middle subtree beta. The left-to-right order alpha, x, beta, y, gamma survives in both pictures, which is what makes the operation a legal local repair to the pointer structure.

interactionPlan.concept: A tree rotation is a local rewiring of the pointer between x and y that hands the middle subtree beta to the opposite side, changing the subtree's shape while preserving the inorder (binary-search) order alpha, x, beta, y, gamma.
elements: left subtree drawing: gray circle y on top with a short parent stub edge rising; y's left edge to gray circle x; y's right edge to leaf label gamma; x's left edge to leaf label alpha; x's right edge to leaf label beta

right subtree drawing: gray circle x on top with a short parent stub edge rising; x's left edge to leaf label alpha; x's right edge to gray circle y; y's left edge to leaf label beta; y's right edge to leaf label gamma
upper dotted arrow pointing leftward, labeled LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)
lower dotted arrow pointing rightward, labeled RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y)
node circles filled light gray with black outline, italic serif labels x and y
Greek leaf labels alpha, beta, gamma at edge ends (no triangles)
inorder strip annotation alpha < x < beta < y < gamma (shown only in Inorder view)

interactions.label: Implement LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)

api.does: returns the node id of i's left child (read-only)
returns the node id of i's right child (read-only)
returns the node id of i's parent (read-only)
make j the left child of i — one of the ONLY ways to mutate
make j the right child of i — one of the ONLY ways to mutate
make j the parent of i — one of the ONLY ways to mutate
attach a learner comment label to node i (annotation only, no structural change)

interactions.frame: the whole 6-node subtree (parent stub P, x, y, alpha, beta, gamma) with the one or two pointers the current assignment just rewired drawn in a highlight color

input.label: Initial tree (right-side config: x on top, y = x.right)
input.default: P.left = x;  x.left = alpha, x.right = y;  y.left = beta, y.right = gamma

interactions.sample_code:
y = right(x)
setRight(x, left(y))   # x.right = beta
setParent(left(y), x)  # beta.p = x
setParent(y, parent(x))# y.p = P
setLeft(parent(x), y)  # P.left = y
setLeft(y, x)          # y.left = x
setParent(x, y)        # x.p = y
interactions.buggy_code:
y = right(x)
setRight(x, left(y))   # x.right = beta
# BUG: forgot setParent(left(y), x), so beta still points up at y
setParent(y, parent(x))
setLeft(parent(x), y)
setLeft(y, x)
setParent(x, y)
interactions.success_check: y is the new top under parent P, x is y's left child, beta is x's right child, alpha is x's left child, gamma is y's right child, and the inorder sequence alpha, x, beta, y, gamma is unchanged
interactions.teaches: Writing the pointer assignments line by line and watching each frame shows exactly which links a rotation touches — the x-y edge flips direction and the middle subtree beta moves to the opposite side — and a wrong assignment visibly breaks the tree or the inorder order

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: In Inorder view the labels read alpha, x, beta, y, gamma left-to-right in BOTH the before and after trees, proving a rotation changes the pointer shape without ever changing the binary-search ordering

demo_steps.title: Two shapes, one local fix
demo_steps.narration: The left and right drawings are the same five items connected differently: LEFT-ROTATE(T, x) turns the right shape into the left one, and RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y) does the reverse. Only the x-y link and the ownership of beta differ.

demo_steps.title: Run the rotation frame by frame
demo_steps.narration: Run the sample leftRotate(x): each pointer assignment advances one frame, moving beta from y's left to x's right and swapping the parent-child roles of x and y. Try the buggy version to watch a missed setParent leave beta dangling.

demo_steps.title: Order is invariant
demo_steps.narration: Switch to Inorder view: the sequence alpha, x, beta, y, gamma reads identically before and after, so the rotation is a legal local repair that reshapes the tree while preserving the binary-search property.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A rotation rewires only the edge between x and y and re-homes the middle subtree beta to the opposite side, so the subtree's shape changes but its inorder order alpha, x, beta, y, gamma — and hence the binary-search property — stays exactly the same.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Lay out two small subtree drawings side by side with the dotted double-arrow block between them, matching CLRS Fig 13.2: left drawing has y on top (parent stub up), x as y's left child, gamma as y's right leaf, alpha and beta as x's leaves; right drawing has x on top (parent stub up), alpha as x's left leaf, y as x's right child, beta and gamma as y's leaves. Node circles light gray fill with thin black outline and italic serif x/y; leaf labels alpha, beta, gamma in italic serif at edge ends with no triangles. Upper dotted arrow points left with 'LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)' above it; lower dotted arrow points right with 'RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y)' below it. During code-editor replay, redraw the whole 6-node subtree each frame and color the just-changed pointer(s) in a bright accent (e.g. red) so the touched links pop. In Inorder view, draw a horizontal strip beneath both trees listing alpha < x < beta < y < gamma with matching node colors to make the preserved ordering obvious; cross-fade this strip in/out on toggle.

authoredContext: The search-tree operations TREE-INSERT and TREE-DELETE, when run on a redblack tree with n keys, take O.lg n/ time. Because they modify the tree, the result may violate the red-black properties enumerated in Section 13.1. To restore these properties, we must change the colors of some of the nodes in the tree and also change the pointer structure. We change the pointer structure through rotation, which is a local operation in a search tree that preserves the binary-search-tree property. Figure 13.2 shows the two kinds of rotations: left rotations and right rotations. When we do a left rotation on a node x, we assume that its right child y is not T:nil; x may be any node in the tree whose right child is not T:nil. The left rotation “pivots” around the link from x to y. It makes y the new root of the subtree, with x as y’s left child and y’s left child as x’s right child.
